properties.natural_language: PRECOND: Before processing data from EXT-RPC-NODE (trust=SEMI_TRUSTED), all input crossing boundary edge EDGE-NODE-RESPONDS into STATE-CAP-RETRIEVED SHALL be validated. The gas cap hex response must be a valid QUANTITY encoding or null. Security assumption: RPC nodes are user-configured but could return incorrect data.

PRECOND: Data items [DATA-GAS-CAP-HEX] flowing across boundary edge EDGE-NODE-RESPONDS from SEMI_TRUSTED entity EXT-RPC-NODE SHALL be integrity-checked and sanitized before any state transition from STATE-CAP-RETRIEVED.

INV: The trust boundary at edge EDGE-NODE-RESPONDS SHALL never be bypassed. All transitions from external entity EXT-RPC-NODE to internal state STATE-CAP-RETRIEVED MUST traverse the validation path. No alternative path may circumvent this boundary.

PRECOND: Before processing data from EXT-RPC-NODE (trust=SEMI_TRUSTED), all input crossing boundary edge EDGE-NODE-NULL into STATE-NO-FINITE-CAP SHALL be validated. A null response indicates no finite cap exists and must be distinguished from error responses.
PRECOND: Action 'Send eth_txGasLimitCap Request' SHALL only be invoked when system is in state 'Client Needs Gas Cap Info'. Client must need gas cap discovery before initiating RPC query.
POSTCOND: After action 'Send eth_txGasLimitCap Request' completes, the system SHALL transition to state 'Awaiting Node Response'. The request has been transmitted to the node.
POSTCOND: After action 'Node Computes Effective Cap', the result SHALL be min(protocolCap, policyCap). The node computes the effective gas limit cap from protocol and policy constraints.

PRECOND [Ambiguity AMB-EIP8123-01]: The relationship between protocolCap and policyCap: policyCap is assumed to apply only to mempool admission, not consensus. Transactions above policyCap but below protocolCap could still be included by other nodes. Implementations SHOULD document this distinction.

PRECOND [Ambiguity AMB-EIP8123-02]: When protocol cap changes at a hard fork, the method returns the current effective cap at query time. Clients SHOULD re-query after known hard forks to obtain updated cap values.

PRECOND [Assumption ASSUM-EIP8123-01]: The system assumes the RPC node is trusted to return accurate cap information. If this assumption is violated, malicious nodes could return incorrect caps causing transaction failures or users to believe they can submit transactions that will be rejected. Implementations SHOULD query multiple nodes.

PRECOND [Assumption ASSUM-EIP8123-02]: Different chains have different protocol caps. Clients MUST NOT hardcode gas limits but instead query per-chain caps via eth_txGasLimitCap to support heterogeneous environments.

PRECOND [Assumption ASSUM-EIP8123-03]: Wallets and tools SHALL query eth_txGasLimitCap instead of hardcoding gas limits. Failure to do so may result in invalid transactions or underutilized gas on chains with different caps.
PRECOND: Action 'Compute Minimum of Caps' SHALL only be invoked when at least one of STATE-PROTOCOL-CAP-DEFINED or STATE-POLICY-CAP-CONFIGURED is active. Both caps feed into the minimum computation.
POSTCOND: After action 'Compute Minimum of Caps', the effective cap SHALL equal min(protocolCap, policyCap). The system transitions to STATE-EFFECTIVE-CAP-COMPUTED.

POSTCOND: After determining no protocol cap exists (STATE-NO-PROTOCOL-CAP) and no policy cap exists (STATE-NO-POLICY-CAP), ACTION-RETURN-NULL SHALL be invoked returning null to indicate no finite cap.

INV: The effective gas cap SHALL always be less than or equal to both the protocol cap and policy cap when both are defined. The minimum function is monotonically non-increasing with respect to either input.

PRECOND: Before processing data from EXT-USER (trust=SEMI_TRUSTED), all input crossing boundary edge EDGE-USER-INITIATES into STATE-WALLET-PREPARING-TX SHALL be validated. User transaction parameters must be well-formed.
PRECOND: Action 'Query Gas Cap' SHALL only be invoked when system is in state 'Wallet Preparing Transaction'. Gas cap discovery occurs during transaction construction.

POSTCOND: After action 'Validate Against Cap' completes, the system SHALL transition to either STATE-TX-WITHIN-CAP (gas <= cap) or STATE-TX-EXCEEDS-CAP (gas > cap). These outcomes are mutually exclusive.
POSTCOND: When transaction exceeds cap (STATE-TX-EXCEEDS-CAP), ACTION-WARN-USER SHALL be invoked to alert the user of the limitation before any submission attempt.
PRECOND: Action 'Estimate Gas Needed' SHALL only be invoked when gas cap is known (STATE-GAS-CAP-KNOWN). Gas estimation requires cap context to provide meaningful results.
POSTCOND: After action 'Query Gas Cap' completes, system SHALL transition to STATE-GAS-CAP-KNOWN with the retrieved cap value available for comparison.

PRECOND: Before processing data from EXT-CALLER (trust=UNTRUSTED), all input crossing boundary edge EDGE-CALL-RECEIVED into STATE-MODEXP-CALL-RECEIVED SHALL be validated. The 1024-byte input limits exist because callers are untrusted. Input validation occurs before expensive computation.

PRECOND: Data items [DATA-INPUT-BUFFER] flowing across boundary edge EDGE-CALL-RECEIVED from UNTRUSTED entity EXT-CALLER SHALL be integrity-checked and size-bounded before any MODEXP computation from STATE-MODEXP-CALL-RECEIVED.

INV: The trust boundary at edge EDGE-CALL-RECEIVED SHALL never be bypassed. All transitions from external entity EXT-CALLER to internal state STATE-MODEXP-CALL-RECEIVED MUST traverse the validation path. No alternative path may circumvent this boundary.
PRECOND: Action 'Parse Length Parameters' SHALL only be invoked when system is in state 'MODEXP Precompile Call Received'. Input must be received before parsing begins.
POSTCOND: After action 'Parse Length Parameters' completes, the system SHALL transition to STATE-LENGTHS-PARSED with all three length values (BASE, EXPONENT, MODULUS) extracted.

INV: For all MODEXP calls, length_of_BASE, length_of_EXPONENT, and length_of_MODULUS SHALL each be <= 1024 bytes (8192 bits). Any violation SHALL result in immediate rejection via STATE-LENGTH-EXCEEDED.
POSTCOND: After any length check action detects a value > 1024 bytes, the system SHALL transition to STATE-LENGTH-EXCEEDED. The check sequence is short-circuit: first failure triggers rejection.
POSTCOND: After all three length checks pass (STATE-ALL-LENGTHS-VALID), ACTION-PROCEED-MODEXP SHALL be invoked to continue with standard EIP-198 computation.
POSTCOND: After STATE-LENGTH-EXCEEDED, ACTION-CONSUME-ALL-GAS SHALL be invoked followed by ACTION-RETURN-ERROR, resulting in STATE-CALL-FAILED. All gas allocated to the call is consumed as penalty.

PRECOND [Ambiguity AMB-EIP7823-01]: The precompile error return format is assumed to follow standard precompile behavior: empty data with execution failure status. Implementations MUST return consistent error format across all clients.

PRECOND [Ambiguity AMB-EIP7823-02]: The length check is assumed to happen early (before complex pricing calculation), with all-gas-consumption penalty applied on violation. Implementations MUST check lengths before computing gas costs.

PRECOND [Assumption ASSUM-EIP7823-01]: Historical blockchain analysis is assumed to accurately represent all legitimate MODEXP use cases. If violated, the 1024-byte limit could break existing applications using larger inputs not captured in historical analysis.

PRECOND [Assumption ASSUM-EIP7823-02]: No legitimate cryptographic operations require inputs larger than 8192 bits. If violated, future cryptographic standards requiring larger keys would be unsupported by MODEXP.

INV [Assumption ASSUM-EIP7823-03]: All client implementations MUST implement the 1024-byte bounds check identically. Divergent implementations would cause consensus failures - the exact problem this EIP aims to prevent.

PRECOND: Before processing data from EXT-ATTACKER (threat actor pattern, trust=UNTRUSTED), all input crossing boundary edge EDGE-ATTACKER-TRIES into ACTION-ATTACKER-SUBMIT-LARGE-INPUT SHALL be validated. Large inputs are immediately rejected at the bounds check stage.

POSTCOND: After STATE-LARGE-INPUT-RECEIVED, ACTION-IMMEDIATE-REJECTION SHALL be invoked, resulting in STATE-ATTACK-MITIGATED. Large input attacks are prevented at the validation stage without complex processing.

INV: Post-EIP7823, the MODEXP precompile SHALL always operate in STATE-BOUNDED-INPUT mode. Bounded inputs create a finite testable domain (STATE-TESTING-DOMAIN-FINITE) and enable future EVMMAX replacement (STATE-EVMMAX-COMPATIBLE).

PRECOND: Before processing data from EXT-CALLER (trust=UNTRUSTED), gas allocation crossing boundary edge EDGE-GAS-PROVIDED into STATE-GAS-ALLOCATED SHALL be tracked. The gas limit data is untrusted input from the caller.

POSTCOND: After ACTION-DETECT-VIOLATION identifies a length > 1024 bytes, the system SHALL transition to STATE-VIOLATION-DETECTED, then ACTION-CHARGE-ALL-GAS SHALL consume all remaining gas, resulting in STATE-GAS-EXHAUSTED and STATE-CALLER-PENALIZED.

INV: When a MODEXP input length violation is detected, ALL gas allocated to the call SHALL be consumed. The caller MUST be economically penalized for submitting invalid inputs. Zero gas refund on violation.

PRECOND: Before processing data from EXT-WHISPER-PEER (trust=UNTRUSTED), all input crossing boundary edge EDGE-PEER-CONNECTS into STATE-HANDSHAKE-PENDING SHALL be validated. Whisper peers are untrusted network participants that may send malformed data or violate protocol requirements.

PRECOND: Before processing data from EXT-WHISPER-PEER (trust=UNTRUSTED), message envelopes crossing boundary edge EDGE-RECEIVE-ENVELOPE into STATE-MESSAGE-RECEIVED SHALL be validated for structure, PoW, and bloom filter match.

INV: The trust boundary at edges EDGE-PEER-CONNECTS and EDGE-RECEIVE-ENVELOPE SHALL never be bypassed. All data from EXT-WHISPER-PEER MUST traverse validation paths. No alternative path may circumvent these boundaries.
PRECOND: Action 'Send Status Message' SHALL only be invoked when system is in state 'Whisper Handshake Pending'. Status exchange must occur before envelope transmission.
POSTCOND: After action 'Send Status Message' completes successfully, the system SHALL transition to STATE-HANDSHAKE-COMPLETE. Both peers have exchanged status messages.

PRECOND: Actions 'Send Message Envelopes', 'Update PoW Requirement', and 'Update Bloom Filter' SHALL only be invoked when system is in state 'Whisper Handshake Complete'. No envelope or parameter exchange before handshake.
PRECOND: Action 'Validate Envelope Structure' SHALL only be invoked when system is in state 'Envelope Received'. Envelope format [Expiry(4), TTL(4), Topic(4), Data(var), Nonce(8)] must be verified.
POSTCOND: After action 'Validate Envelope Structure' completes successfully, ACTION-VALIDATE-POW SHALL be invoked next. Structure validation precedes PoW verification.

INV: Envelope validation SHALL follow a strict sequential order: Structure -> PoW -> Bloom Filter. Any failure at any stage SHALL result in STATE-ENVELOPE-REJECTED. Invalid PoW values (NaN, INF, negative) MUST be rejected.

POSTCOND: After ACTION-CHECK-BLOOM-MATCH determines topic matches interest filter, envelope SHALL transition to STATE-ENVELOPE-ACCEPTED. Non-matching topics transition to STATE-ENVELOPE-REJECTED (silently dropped).
POSTCOND: When STATE-ENVELOPE-REJECTED is reached due to severe protocol violation, ACTION-DISCONNECT-PEER SHALL be invoked to terminate the connection with the misbehaving peer.

PRECOND: Before processing data from EXT-APPLICATION (trust=SEMI_TRUSTED), plaintext message crossing boundary edge EDGE-APP-SENDS-MESSAGE into STATE-PLAINTEXT-MESSAGE SHALL be encrypted before transmission.

PRECOND: Before processing data from EXT-WHISPER-PEER (trust=UNTRUSTED), encrypted envelopes crossing boundary edge EDGE-RECEIVE-ENCRYPTED into STATE-RECEIVED-ENCRYPTED SHALL be validated and decrypted using available keys.
INV: All messages transmitted over the Whisper network SHALL be encrypted using either ECIES (asymmetric) or AES-GCM (symmetric). Plaintext messages SHALL never leave the local node boundary.

POSTCOND: After encryption (ECIES or AES-GCM), ACTION-SIGN-MESSAGE SHALL sign with ECDSA, then ACTION-PAD-MESSAGE SHALL apply 256-byte alignment padding, resulting in STATE-ENCRYPTED-ENVELOPE ready for transmission.
POSTCOND: After ACTION-DECRYPT-MESSAGE successfully decrypts an envelope, system SHALL transition to STATE-DECRYPTED-MESSAGE with verified authenticity.
INV: Message padding SHALL always align to 256-byte boundaries to prevent size-based metadata leakage. This SHALL apply uniformly to all messages regardless of encryption type.
PRECOND [Ambiguity AMB-EIP627-01]: The bloom filter uses 3 hash functions mapping topics to 512-bit space. Implementations MUST use consistent hashing to ensure correct topic filtering across nodes.

PRECOND [Ambiguity AMB-EIP627-03]: Unknown packet codes MUST be silently ignored, but malformed packets (invalid encoding) SHOULD be rejected. Implementations MUST distinguish between unknown-but-valid and malformed packets.

PRECOND [Assumption ASSUM-EIP627-01]: Attackers cannot break ECIES or AES-GCM encryption within the message TTL timeframe. If violated, message confidentiality would be compromised. Implementations SHOULD use strong key material.

PRECOND [Assumption ASSUM-EIP627-02]: The bloom filter is assumed to provide sufficient privacy to hide exact topic interests. If violated, attackers could correlate bloom filter patterns with specific topics, enabling traffic analysis.
PRECOND [Assumption ASSUM-EIP627-03]: Sufficient network peers must exist to provide anonymity through message mixing. If violated, message origin could be determined through timing analysis.

PRECOND: Before processing data from EXT-USER (trust=SEMI_TRUSTED), all input crossing boundary edge EDGE-TX-RECEIVED into STATE-SET-CODE-TX-RECEIVED SHALL be validated. Transaction submitter is semi-trusted - each authorization requires valid ECDSA signature from authority EOA.

PRECOND: Data items [DATA-SET-CODE-TX, DATA-AUTHORIZATION-LIST] flowing across boundary edge EDGE-TX-RECEIVED from SEMI_TRUSTED entity EXT-USER SHALL be validated including transaction type (0x05), signature, and each authorization tuple.

INV: The trust boundary at edge EDGE-TX-RECEIVED SHALL never be bypassed. All SET_CODE transactions from EXT-USER MUST traverse the full validation chain (chain ID -> nonce bounds -> authority recovery -> account nonce -> code check) before delegation is applied.
PRECOND: Action 'Process Authorization List' SHALL only be invoked when system is in state 'SET_CODE Transaction Received'. Each authorization is processed sequentially.
POSTCOND: After ACTION-VALIDATE-CHAIN-ID, if chain_id does not match current chain and is not 0 (universal), the system SHALL transition to STATE-AUTHORIZATION-SKIPPED. No error is raised.
POSTCOND: After ACTION-VALIDATE-NONCE-BOUNDS, if nonce >= U64.MAX, the system SHALL transition to STATE-AUTHORIZATION-SKIPPED. Nonce overflow prevention.
POSTCOND: After ACTION-RECOVER-AUTHORITY, if signature recovery fails, the system SHALL transition to STATE-AUTHORIZATION-SKIPPED. Invalid signatures are silently skipped.
POSTCOND: After ACTION-VALIDATE-ACCOUNT-NONCE, if account nonce does not match authorization nonce, the system SHALL transition to STATE-AUTHORIZATION-SKIPPED.

POSTCOND: After ACTION-VALIDATE-EXISTING-CODE, if account has non-empty non-delegation code, the system SHALL transition to STATE-AUTHORIZATION-SKIPPED. Only empty or existing delegation code is acceptable.

POSTCOND: After successful validation, ACTION-SET-DELEGATION-CODE SHALL set account code to 0xef0100 + target_address, then ACTION-INCREMENT-NONCE SHALL increment authority nonce by 1, resulting in STATE-DELEGATION-ACTIVE.
INV: Failed authorization validations SHALL always result in STATE-AUTHORIZATION-SKIPPED (silent skip), never in transaction rejection. The transaction continues processing remaining authorizations.
PRECOND: Action 'Validate Y Parity' SHALL only be invoked when system is in state 'Authorization Received'. Signature components (y_parity, r, s) must be present.

INV: Signature validation SHALL follow strict sequential order: y_parity -> r range -> s range -> hash computation -> ECDSA recovery. Any failure at any stage SHALL result in STATE-INVALID-SIGNATURE (InvalidSignatureError).
INV: y_parity SHALL be exactly 0 or 1. r and s SHALL be within the secp256k1 curve order (0 < r < n, 0 < s < n). The signing hash SHALL be keccak256(0x05 || RLP(chain_id, address, nonce)).
POSTCOND: After ACTION-ECRECOVER succeeds, system SHALL transition to STATE-AUTHORITY-RECOVERED with the valid authority address. After failure, system SHALL transition to STATE-INVALID-SIGNATURE.
PRECOND: Action 'Check Accessed Addresses' SHALL only be invoked when system is in state 'Delegation Access Requested'. Address warm/cold status must be determined before gas computation.

POSTCOND: After ACTION-CHECK-ACCESS-SET, system SHALL transition to either STATE-ADDRESS-WARM (previously accessed, 100 gas) or STATE-ADDRESS-COLD (first access, 2600 gas). These outcomes are mutually exclusive.
POSTCOND: After ACTION-COMPUTE-ACCESS-GAS, ACTION-UPDATE-ACCESS-SET SHALL add the address to the accessed_addresses warm set, resulting in STATE-ACCESS-COMPLETE.
INV: Warm access cost SHALL always be 100 gas and cold access cost SHALL always be 2600 gas. Once an address is added to accessed_addresses, all subsequent accesses SHALL be warm.
PRECOND: Action 'Check Code Length' SHALL only be invoked when system is in state 'Code Received for Validation'. Bytecode must be available for length check.
INV: Valid delegation code SHALL be exactly 23 bytes (EOA_DELEGATED_CODE_LENGTH) and SHALL start with 0xef0100 (EOA_DELEGATION_MARKER). Any deviation SHALL result in STATE-INVALID-DELEGATION.
POSTCOND: After ACTION-EXTRACT-TARGET successfully extracts the 20-byte address, system SHALL transition to STATE-VALID-DELEGATION with the target address available.
PRECOND [Ambiguity AMB-EOA-DELEG-01]: Setting delegation to NULL_ADDRESS (0x0000...0000) is assumed to clear delegation (empty code, length 0). Implementations MUST treat NULL_ADDRESS as revocation.

PRECOND [Ambiguity AMB-EOA-DELEG-02]: Multiple authorizations for the same authority in a single transaction are assumed to be processed in order. Later authorizations will fail nonce check due to prior increment.

PRECOND [Ambiguity AMB-EOA-DELEG-03]: Any 20-byte address is assumed valid as delegation target, including EOAs and non-existent accounts. Implementations SHOULD NOT reject based on target account existence.
PRECOND [Assumption ASSUM-EOA-DELEG-01]: Attackers cannot forge ECDSA signatures to create unauthorized delegations. If violated, attackers could hijack EOAs by forging delegation authorizations.

PRECOND [Assumption ASSUM-EOA-DELEG-02]: The delegation target contract is assumed trusted by the EOA owner at authorization time. If violated, users could delegate to malicious contracts that steal funds.

INV [Assumption ASSUM-EOA-DELEG-03]: The secp256k1 curve parameters used for ECDSA SHALL be correct and consistent across all implementations. Divergent parameters would cause signature validation discrepancies between nodes.

PRECOND [Assumption ASSUM-EOA-DELEG-04]: Users are assumed to understand that delegating code changes their EOA's behavior for all future transactions. If violated, users may unintentionally lock themselves out.

INV [Assumption ASSUM-EOA-DELEG-05]: The 0xef0100 marker (3 bytes) SHALL uniquely identify delegation code and SHALL NOT conflict with valid EVM bytecode. This is guaranteed by EIP-3541 (0xEF byte reservation).

PRECOND: Before processing data from EXT-CONSENSUS-LAYER (trust=TRUSTED), beacon root data crossing boundary edge EDGE-CL-PROVIDES-ROOT into STATE-BLOCK-PROCESSING-START SHALL be accepted as authenticated. The CL is cryptographically authenticated via proof-of-stake.

INV: The trust boundary at edge EDGE-CL-PROVIDES-ROOT represents a TRUSTED system input. The execution layer SHALL unconditionally accept beacon block roots from the consensus layer without independent verification. This is a fundamental trust assumption of the merged architecture.
PRECOND: Action 'Extract Parent Beacon Block Root' SHALL only be invoked when system is in state 'Block Processing Started'. Beacon root processing occurs before any user transactions.
POSTCOND: After ACTION-COMPUTE-STORAGE-INDEX, the storage index SHALL equal (timestamp % 8191). The ring buffer has HISTORY_BUFFER_LENGTH = 8191 slots.

POSTCOND: After ACTION-SYSTEM-CALL-BEACON-CONTRACT, ACTION-STORE-TIMESTAMP SHALL write the block timestamp at the computed index, then ACTION-STORE-BEACON-ROOT SHALL write the beacon root at index + HISTORY_BUFFER_LENGTH.
INV: For every stored beacon root, the corresponding timestamp SHALL be stored at index (timestamp % 8191) and the root SHALL be stored at index + 8191. Both values MUST be written atomically.

PRECOND: Before processing data from EXT-CALLING-CONTRACT (trust=UNTRUSTED), all input crossing boundary edge EDGE-CONTRACT-QUERY into STATE-QUERY-RECEIVED SHALL be validated. Contracts may attempt to query invalid timestamps or exploit ring buffer wraparound.
PRECOND: Data items [DATA-QUERY-TIMESTAMP] flowing across boundary edge EDGE-CONTRACT-QUERY from UNTRUSTED entity EXT-CALLING-CONTRACT SHALL be validated: exactly 32 bytes and non-zero.
INV: Query validation SHALL follow: input length (32 bytes) -> non-zero check -> compute index -> load stored timestamp -> timestamp match. Any failure SHALL result in STATE-QUERY-REVERTED.
POSTCOND: After ACTION-VALIDATE-TIMESTAMP-MATCH succeeds (queried timestamp == stored timestamp), ACTION-LOAD-BEACON-ROOT SHALL retrieve the beacon root and system transitions to STATE-QUERY-SUCCESS.
POSTCOND: After ACTION-VALIDATE-TIMESTAMP-MATCH fails (timestamp mismatch), system SHALL transition to STATE-QUERY-REVERTED. Stale or missing data is rejected.
PRECOND: The CL block must be finalized (STATE-CL-BLOCK-FINALIZED) before ACTION-EMBED-ROOT-IN-HEADER can embed the root in the execution header. Unfinalized roots are not propagated.

POSTCOND: After ACTION-EMBED-ROOT-IN-HEADER, the beacon root is part of the execution header (STATE-ROOT-IN-EL-HEADER). After ACTION-VALIDATE-ROOT-FROM-CL, it becomes STATE-ROOT-TRUSTED without independent EL verification.
PRECOND: Action 'Allocate System Call Gas' SHALL only be invoked when system is in state 'System Call Initiated'. The 30M gas allocation is separate from block gas limit.
INV: System call gas allocation SHALL be exactly 30,000,000 gas, SHALL NOT be deducted from block gas limit, and SHALL have value=0 with no EIP-1559 burn semantics.
POSTCOND: After ACTION-EXECUTE-SYSTEM-CALL, system SHALL transition to either STATE-CALL-SUCCESS or STATE-CALL-SILENT-FAIL. Silent failure (no code at address) SHALL NOT halt block processing.

PRECOND [Ambiguity AMB-EIP4788-01]: The EL unconditionally trusts the CL. If a malicious CL root is included, the EL inherits that compromise. This is a fundamental trust assumption of the merged architecture.

PRECOND [Ambiguity AMB-EIP4788-02]: Queries for pre-fork timestamps will fail timestamp match validation since no data was stored before activation. Implementations SHOULD NOT special-case pre-fork queries.
PRECOND [Ambiguity AMB-EIP4788-03]: Silent failure when no code exists at beacon roots address means the call returns without error and has no effect. Block processing continues normally.

INV [Assumption ASSUM-EIP4788-02]: Block timestamps SHALL be monotonically increasing and reasonably accurate. Timestamp manipulation could cause ring buffer collisions, overwriting recent beacon roots with stale ones.

PRECOND [Assumption ASSUM-EIP4788-03]: The beacon roots contract at BEACON_ROOTS_ADDRESS MUST be correctly deployed with the specified bytecode. Missing or incorrect contract causes silent failures breaking all beacon root dependent functionality.

INV [Assumption ASSUM-EIP4788-04]: An attacker SHALL NOT be able to produce valid execution blocks without corresponding consensus layer blocks. This prevents injection of arbitrary beacon roots into the EVM.

PRECOND: Before processing data from EXT-TX-SUBMITTER (trust=UNTRUSTED), all input crossing boundary edge EDGE-RECEIVE-TX into STATE-TX-RECEIVED SHALL be validated. Full transaction validation required including EIP-2718 envelope format and type namespace.

PRECOND: Data items [DATA-RAW-TX] flowing across boundary edge EDGE-RECEIVE-TX from UNTRUSTED entity EXT-TX-SUBMITTER SHALL be integrity-checked including transaction type byte and namespace validity.
INV: The trust boundary at edge EDGE-RECEIVE-TX SHALL never be bypassed. All transactions from EXT-TX-SUBMITTER MUST traverse validation including type extraction and namespace check.
PRECOND: Action 'Extract Transaction Type' SHALL only be invoked when system is in state 'Transaction Received'. Type byte must be parsed from the transaction envelope.
POSTCOND: After ACTION-EXTRACT-TX-TYPE completes, system SHALL transition to STATE-TX-TYPE-IDENTIFIED. The transaction type byte is available for namespace classification.
POSTCOND: After ACTION-CHECK-RIP-RANGE, system SHALL transition to either STATE-TX-TYPE-RIP (type in 0x40-0x7f) or STATE-TX-TYPE-EIP (type outside RIP range). These outcomes are mutually exclusive.

INV: Transaction types in the range 0x40-0x7f (inclusive) SHALL be reserved for RIP definitions. Types outside this range SHALL be handled by EIP standards. The boundary values 0x40 and 0x7f are both inclusive.
PRECOND: Action 'Validate EIP-2718 Compliance' SHALL only be invoked when system is in state 'Transaction Pending Type Validation'. Envelope format must be verified first.
POSTCOND: After ACTION-VALIDATE-EIP2718-COMPLIANCE succeeds, ACTION-VALIDATE-NAMESPACE-AUTHORITY SHALL verify the type is defined by the appropriate authority (EIP vs RIP).

POSTCOND: After ACTION-VALIDATE-NAMESPACE-AUTHORITY, system SHALL transition to STATE-TX-TYPE-VALID (type defined by appropriate authority) or STATE-TX-TYPE-UNKNOWN (type not defined in any namespace).
PRECOND: Action 'Route by Transaction Type' SHALL accept transactions from both L1 (STATE-L1-TX-CONTEXT) and L2 (STATE-L2-TX-CONTEXT) contexts. Routing is based on type namespace only.
POSTCOND: After ACTION-ROUTE-BY-TYPE, types < 0x40 or > 0x7f SHALL route to STATE-EIP-PROCESSING, types in 0x40-0x7f SHALL route to STATE-RIP-PROCESSING. Routing is deterministic.

PRECOND [Ambiguity AMB-EIP7808-01]: Conflicts between different RIPs using the same transaction type in the reserved range are assumed to be resolved by RIP governance. Implementations SHOULD validate against known RIP type allocations.
PRECOND [Assumption ASSUM-EIP7808-01]: The RIP governance process is assumed to responsibly allocate transaction types. If violated, conflicting types could cause interoperability issues between L2s.

INV [Assumption ASSUM-EIP7808-02]: The 64-value range (0x40-0x7f) SHALL be sufficient for all future L2 transaction type needs. Range exhaustion would require protocol changes to expand the RIP namespace.

INV [Assumption ASSUM-EIP7808-03]: L1 nodes SHALL NOT attempt to process RIP transaction types as if they were EIP types. Invalid processing or crashes when encountering RIP transactions MUST be prevented.
PRECOND: Action 'Patricialize Trie' SHALL only be invoked when system is in state 'Trie Initialized'. The trie must have secured flag, default value, and backing data configured.

POSTCOND: After ACTION-PATRICIALIZE completes, the trie SHALL be organized into STATE-NODE-LEAF, STATE-NODE-EXTENSION, and STATE-NODE-BRANCH nodes with compression optimization, resulting in STATE-TRIE-STRUCTURED.

INV: The trie SHALL contain exactly three node types: Leaf (terminal key-value), Extension (shared prefix compression), and Branch (16-way divergence with optional value). No other node types are permitted.
PRECOND: Actions 'Trie Set', 'Trie Get', and 'Copy Trie' SHALL only be invoked when system is in state 'Trie Ready for Operations'. The trie must be initialized before operations.
POSTCOND: After ACTION-TRIE-SET, if the value differs from default, system SHALL transition to STATE-KEY-SET. If value equals default, system SHALL transition to STATE-KEY-DELETED (key removed).
POSTCOND: After ACTION-TRIE-GET, if key exists system SHALL transition to STATE-VALUE-RETRIEVED. If key is absent, system SHALL transition to STATE-DEFAULT-RETURNED.
POSTCOND: After ACTION-COPY-TRIE, system SHALL create a shallow copy (STATE-TRIE-COPIED) leveraging frozen object semantics. The copy is safe because underlying data is immutable.
PRECOND: Action 'Prepare Trie Data' SHALL only be invoked when system is in state 'Trie Data Ready for Root Computation'. All key-value pairs must be present before root computation begins.

POSTCOND: After ACTION-PREPARE-TRIE, values are encoded, keys conditionally hashed (if secured), and converted to nibble format (STATE-TRIE-PREPARED). ACTION-BUILD-TREE then creates the Patricia tree (STATE-TREE-BUILT).
POSTCOND: After ACTION-ENCODE-ROOT, the final root node is compressed via RLP and hashed with Keccak-256 if >= 32 bytes, producing STATE-ROOT-COMPUTED with the 32-byte root hash.
POSTCOND: When trie is empty (STATE-TRIE-DATA-READY with no entries), system SHALL immediately return STATE-EMPTY-TRIE-ROOT (EMPTY_TRIE_ROOT constant) without building a tree.
PRECOND: Action 'Convert Nibbles to Compact' SHALL only be invoked when system is in state 'Nibble List Ready'. Keys must be in 4-bit representation before compact encoding.
POSTCOND: After ACTION-NIBBLE-TO-COMPACT, nibbles are compressed with parity (bit 0) and node type (bit 1) flags, producing STATE-COMPACT-ENCODED.
POSTCOND: After ACTION-ENCODE-INTERNAL-NODE, if RLP encoding < 32 bytes, node is returned inline (STATE-NODE-INLINE). If >= 32 bytes, Keccak-256 hash is returned (STATE-NODE-HASHED).

INV: The 32-byte threshold for node hashing SHALL be strictly applied. Nodes with RLP encoding < 32 bytes are inline; nodes >= 32 bytes are replaced by their Keccak-256 hash. This threshold is non-configurable.
PRECOND [Ambiguity AMB-CANCUN-TRIE-01]: The secured flag SHALL be true for state and storage tries (preventing key preimage attacks) and false for transaction/receipt tries (sequential index keys).
INV [Assumption ASSUM-CANCUN-TRIE-01]: Keccak-256 SHALL be collision-resistant. Hash collisions could allow state forgery, enabling arbitrary balance modifications or contract storage manipulation.
INV [Assumption ASSUM-CANCUN-TRIE-02]: Attackers SHALL NOT be able to compute preimages for hashed keys in secured tries. Preimage attacks could enable targeted state slot manipulation.

INV [Assumption ASSUM-CANCUN-TRIE-03]: RLP encoding SHALL be deterministic, producing identical bytes for identical inputs across all implementations. Non-deterministic encoding would cause root hash mismatches and consensus failures.
PRECOND: Before processing data from EXT-GAS-CALCULATOR (reclassified as INTERNAL_COMPONENT), memory size values entering STATE-MEMORY-SIZE-INPUT SHALL be non-negative unsigned integers.

POSTCOND: After ACTION-CHECK-ALIGNMENT, if remainder is 0, system returns original value via STATE-ALREADY-ALIGNED. If non-zero, ACTION-ROUND-UP-TO-32 adds (32 - remainder). Both paths produce STATE-ALIGNED-VALUE-PRODUCED.
INV: ceil32 output SHALL always be a multiple of 32 and SHALL always be >= the input value. The function is monotonically non-decreasing.

PRECOND: Before processing data from EXT-FEE-MARKET (reclassified as INTERNAL_COMPONENT), parameters (factor, numerator, denominator) entering STATE-EXP-PARAMS-RECEIVED SHALL have denominator > 0 to prevent division by zero.
POSTCOND: After ACTION-INIT-TAYLOR-SERIES, the system enters STATE-TAYLOR-ITERATION with initial accumulator = factor * denominator. The loop computes successive Taylor series terms.
POSTCOND: After ACTION-CHECK-CONVERGENCE, if numerator term is still positive, system loops back to STATE-TAYLOR-ITERATION. If zero, system transitions to STATE-CONVERGED then ACTION-FINALIZE-RESULT.
INV: The Taylor series SHALL always converge (terminate) for valid inputs. The factorial denominator growth guarantees convergence. The result approximates factor * e^(numerator/denominator).
PRECOND: Before processing data from EXT-CRYPTO-OP (reclassified as INTERNAL_COMPONENT), raw bytes entering STATE-BYTES-INPUT SHALL have length divisible by 4 for proper U32 chunking.
POSTCOND: After ACTION-CHUNK-BYTES and ACTION-CONVERT-LE-TO-U32, system SHALL produce STATE-U32-SEQUENCE-PRODUCED with each 4-byte chunk interpreted as little-endian U32.
POSTCOND: After ACTION-CONVERT-U32-TO-LE and ACTION-CONCATENATE-BYTES, system SHALL produce STATE-BYTES-OUTPUT-PRODUCED with fixed-length output (4 bytes per U32) regardless of leading zeros.

INV: Byte-to-U32 and U32-to-byte conversions SHALL be inverse operations. le_bytes_to_uint32_sequence(le_uint32_sequence_to_bytes(x)) == x for all valid inputs. Round-trip integrity is required for cryptographic correctness.
PRECOND: Before processing data from EXT-VALIDATOR (reclassified as INTERNAL_COMPONENT), numeric values entering STATE-NUMBER-TO-VALIDATE SHALL be convertible to standard integer type.
POSTCOND: After ACTION-CHECK-PRIMALITY using trial division, system SHALL transition to STATE-IS-PRIME (no divisors found for 2..sqrt(n)) or STATE-NOT-PRIME (divisor found or n <= 1).
POSTCOND: After ACTION-DETERMINE-SIGN, system SHALL transition to exactly one of: STATE-SIGN-NEGATIVE (value < 0), STATE-SIGN-ZERO (value == 0), or STATE-SIGN-POSITIVE (value > 0).

INV [Assumption ASSUM-NUMERIC-01]: Integer division behavior SHALL be consistent across all Ethereum client implementations (floor division). Different rounding modes could cause gas calculation discrepancies and consensus failures.

INV [Assumption ASSUM-NUMERIC-04]: Little-endian byte ordering SHALL be consistently applied across all platforms and implementations. Endianness mismatch would corrupt cryptographic operations and cause consensus failures.
PRECOND: Action 'Load Genesis Configuration' SHALL only be invoked when system is in state 'No Blockchain Exists'. Chain initialization occurs exactly once.
POSTCOND: After ACTION-LOAD-GENESIS-CONFIG, system SHALL transition to STATE-CONFIG-LOADED with chain_id, difficulty, gas_limit and other parameters populated from the genesis JSON file.
POSTCOND: After ACTION-POPULATE-INITIAL-ACCOUNTS, system SHALL transition to STATE-ACCOUNTS-POPULATED with all pre-allocated accounts having correct balances, code, and storage in the state trie.

POSTCOND: After ACTION-CREATE-GENESIS-HEADER, system SHALL produce STATE-GENESIS-HEADER-CREATED with zero parent hash, computed state root, and genesis parameters. Then ACTION-APPEND-GENESIS-BLOCK creates block 0 (STATE-CHAIN-INITIALIZED).
INV: The genesis block SHALL always be block number 0 with parent hash equal to zero (32 zero bytes). The genesis block is created exactly once per chain initialization.
PRECOND: Action 'Parse Hexadecimal Values' SHALL only be invoked when system is in state 'Raw Configuration Read'. JSON data must be loaded before hex parsing begins.
POSTCOND: After ACTION-PARSE-HEX-VALUES, if conversion succeeds, system transitions to STATE-VALUES-PARSED. If invalid hex format, system transitions to STATE-PARSE-ERROR.
POSTCOND: After ACTION-VALIDATE-ADDRESSES, if all addresses are valid B_20 (20-byte), system transitions to STATE-ADDRESSES-VALID. Invalid addresses transition to STATE-PARSE-ERROR.
POSTCOND: When STATE-PARSE-ERROR is reached, ACTION-RAISE-EXCEPTION SHALL halt initialization. Invalid genesis configuration MUST prevent node startup.
PRECOND: Action 'Check Fork Type' SHALL only be invoked when system is in state 'Building Genesis Header'. Fork detection determines which header fields to include.

POSTCOND: After ACTION-CHECK-FORK-TYPE, system SHALL transition to the appropriate fork state(s): STATE-PRE-LONDON-FORK (no base fee), STATE-POST-LONDON-FORK (base fee), STATE-POST-SHANGHAI-FORK (withdrawals), STATE-POST-CANCUN-FORK (blob gas).

POSTCOND: Post-London forks SHALL include base_fee_per_gas (ACTION-ADD-BASE-FEE). Post-Shanghai SHALL include empty withdrawals root (ACTION-ADD-WITHDRAWALS-ROOT). Post-Cancun SHALL include blob gas fields (ACTION-ADD-BLOB-FIELDS).
PRECOND [Ambiguity AMB-GENESIS-01]: The genesis nonce 0x42 is assumed mandatory for mainnet compatibility. Other networks may use different values.
PRECOND [Ambiguity AMB-GENESIS-02]: hex_or_base_10_str_to_u256() SHALL interpret 0x-prefixed strings as hex and non-prefixed strings as decimal. '10' parses as decimal 10, not hex 16.
INV [Assumption ASSUM-GENESIS-01]: The genesis configuration file SHALL be trusted and untampered. A malicious genesis file could pre-allocate funds to attacker addresses or set dangerous parameters.
INV [Assumption ASSUM-GENESIS-03]: All nodes on the network SHALL use the same genesis configuration for the target chain_id. Different configurations cause consensus failure and network split.

PRECOND: Before processing data from EXT-WALLET-EXTENSION (trust=UNTRUSTED), all input crossing boundary edge EDGE-WALLET-INJECTION into STATE-WALLET-INJECTED SHALL be treated as potentially malicious. Injected provider code cannot be trusted.

PRECOND: Data items [DATA-PROVIDER-CODE] flowing across boundary edge EDGE-WALLET-INJECTION from UNTRUSTED entity EXT-WALLET-EXTENSION SHALL be defensively handled: freeze provider objects, validate UUID, detect duplicates, and render icons safely.

INV: The trust boundary at edge EDGE-WALLET-INJECTION SHALL never be bypassed. All wallet extension code from EXT-WALLET-EXTENSION MUST be treated as potentially malicious and pass defensive measures.
PRECOND: Action 'Dispatch Request Provider Event' SHALL only be invoked when system is in state 'DApp Page Loaded'. Provider discovery starts after page load.
POSTCOND: After ACTION-DISPATCH-REQUEST-PROVIDER, system SHALL transition to STATE-AWAITING-ANNOUNCEMENTS. DApp begins listening for eip6963:announceProvider events.

POSTCOND: After wallet dispatches announcement (ACTION-DISPATCH-ANNOUNCE-PROVIDER -> STATE-PROVIDER-ANNOUNCED), DApp receives via ACTION-RECEIVE-ANNOUNCEMENT, then ACTION-PERSIST-PROVIDER-DETAIL stores it, resulting in STATE-PROVIDERS-COLLECTED.
PRECOND: Action 'Validate UUID Format' SHALL only be invoked when system is in state 'Provider Info Received'. UUID must be UUIDv4 compliant for session-level uniqueness.

INV: Provider info validation SHALL follow strict order: UUID -> RDNS -> Icon -> Duplicate Detection. All fields MUST pass for STATE-PROVIDER-INFO-VALID. Duplicate UUID SHALL result in STATE-PROVIDER-INFO-SUSPICIOUS (potential impersonation).
POSTCOND: After ACTION-DETECT-DUPLICATE-UUID finds no duplicates, system SHALL transition to STATE-PROVIDER-INFO-VALID. Duplicate UUID found SHALL transition to STATE-PROVIDER-INFO-SUSPICIOUS.

PRECOND: Before processing data from EXT-MALICIOUS-EXTENSION (trust=UNTRUSTED), malicious code crossing boundary edge EDGE-EXTENSION-INJECTS into STATE-UNTRUSTED-EXTENSION-CODE SHALL be mitigated via Object.freeze() and safe rendering.

POSTCOND: After ACTION-FREEZE-PROVIDER-DETAIL applies Object.freeze(), system SHALL transition to STATE-PROVIDER-DETAIL-FROZEN. Frozen objects prevent prototype pollution and post-dispatch modification.
POSTCOND: After ACTION-RENDER-SVG-SAFELY renders SVG icon via tag only, system SHALL transition to STATE-SVG-RENDERED-SAFE. Script execution from SVG is blocked.
INV: SVG icons SHALL NEVER be rendered inline (which would enable STATE-SVG-SCRIPT-EXECUTED attack). All SVG rendering MUST use tag to block script execution.
POSTCOND: After ACTION-PROTOTYPE-POLLUTION-ATTEMPT against frozen objects, system SHALL transition to STATE-POLLUTION-BLOCKED. Object.freeze() prevents runtime modification.
PRECOND [Ambiguity AMB-EIP6963-01]: DApp listeners SHALL persist for page lifetime, meaning until navigation away from origin or page unload. SPAs SHOULD maintain listeners across route changes.
PRECOND [Ambiguity AMB-EIP6963-02]: The rdns field is advisory only and DApps cannot verify domain ownership. Treat rdns as a hint, not a security guarantee.

PRECOND [Assumption ASSUM-EIP6963-01]: DApps trust that the EIP-1193 provider in EIP6963ProviderDetail is legitimate. If violated, a malicious extension could substitute a fake provider stealing keys or redirecting transactions.

PRECOND [Assumption ASSUM-EIP6963-02]: Attackers are assumed unable to inject code before legitimate wallets announce. If violated, fast-loading malicious extensions could impersonate legitimate wallets.

INV [Assumption ASSUM-EIP6963-04]: Users are assumed able to distinguish legitimate from impersonating wallet providers. If violated, users may select malicious impersonators with similar names and icons.
